narrative.overview:
Gantry's design system is the substrate beneath the stack: invisible until you need it, then unmistakably precise. Every token, rule, and component derives from one premise — the interface is infrastructure. It does not perform. It does not decorate. It measures.

The dominant surface is Void Slate (#0B0F14), the near-absolute dark against which Signal Green (#00E599) reads as a live telemetry pulse. Blueprint grid lines appear at 9% opacity across hero sections to suggest a coordinate system without naming one. Corner brackets mark boundaries as a surveyor marks a site. The vocabulary is borrowed from precision instruments: tick marks, readings, traces, output lines.

This system explicitly rejects Generic AI SaaS (purple gradients, glowing orb hero sections, particle mesh), Startup Hustle (testimonial carousels, emoji in headings, unverified social proof badges), and Enterprise Heavy (navy/white palette, compliance logo grids, sales-speak). Gantry is developer-led and earns attention through specificity.
keyCharacteristics: Near-absolute dark background with five tonal surface steps for depth
Single saturated accent (Signal Green) used sparingly as a live-data signal
Monospace type for all data output; display/body pair for headings and prose
2-3px corner radii throughout — machined, not rounded
Blueprint aesthetic: hairline grids, corner brackets, coordinate labels
Motion measured in milliseconds, state changes only; 180ms standard duration

rules.name: The Signal Scarcity Rule
rules.body: Signal Green appears on ≤15% of any screen. Its rarity is what makes it mean 'live data.' When Signal Green loses rarity, it becomes wallpaper. If you count more than three distinct Signal Green elements in a single viewport, remove the least critical one.

rules.name: The Text Floor Rule
rules.body: The floor for body-size text is Text 2 (rgba(255,255,255,0.56)) on a Void Slate background. Text 3 is permitted only for labels in monospace at ≥11px with wide letter-spacing. Text 4 is never for reading.

rules.name: The Mono-as-Instrument Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono is used exclusively for data output: labels, coordinates, code, status messages. Never for headings or prose. When the reader sees monospace, they are reading a measurement or an identifier — not a sentence.

rules.name: The Heading Ceiling Rule
rules.body: Display headings cap at 60px. Section headings cap at 40px. The page does not shout. Letter-spacing floor on display: -0.005em.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: Cards, rows, and list items are flat at rest. A shadow does not appear because something is important; it appears because something is physically lifted. Importance is signaled by Signal Green, not by blur radius.

dos: Do use Signal Green for live data, active states, and success signals. Reserve it — its scarcity makes it trustworthy.
Do step through the five background tiers to create depth without decorative shadows.
Do keep border-radius at 2px for interactive elements and 3px maximum for large containers.
Do write copy in developer vocabulary: specific nouns, concrete verbs, real numbers.
Do use JetBrains Mono exclusively for data output. Never for prose.
Do test body text (Text 2 on Void Slate) for WCAG AA contrast before shipping.
Do include @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) for every animation.
Do use text-wrap: balance on h1/h2 and text-wrap: pretty on prose blocks.
donts: Don't use purple gradients, glowing orb hero sections, particle mesh backgrounds, or animated abstract blobs.
Don't add emoji to headings, use confetti effects, or show testimonial carousels.
Don't use navy/white corporate palette, compliance logo grids, or phrases like 'enterprise-grade' or 'mission-critical'.
Don't pair a 1px border with a box-shadow blur ≥16px on the same element.
Don't increase border-radius above 3px on cards or containers.
Don't use background-clip: text with a gradient.
Don't put monospace eyebrows above every section as structural scaffolding.
Don't write aphoristic-cadence copy (serious statement, then punchy short negation).
Don't use Signal Green as a surface background for non-button elements.
